title: Beat-1 Strum Readiness and Chord-Change Timing for Beginners (JustinGuitar)
summary: In this beginner-focused guitar lesson, JustinGuitar emphasizes the importance of getting chord shapes ready to hit the downbeat (beat 1) when strumming in 4/4 time. He demonstrates how to time chord changes so the new shape is ready for the next beat, uses an E→A example to illustrate one-strum-per-bar rhythm, and explains how players (including left-handed learners) can adjust the timing by starting changes around beat 3 if needed. The video also covers practicing with beat awareness: counting 1-2-3-4, tapping the foot, and optionally changing on beat 4 to improve rhythm. The takeaway is to prioritize a confident beat-1 strum and to use deliberate chord-change planning to sound musical while you learn.
topics: E to A chord progression example
Starting chord changes after beat 4 (beat-4 change)
Avoiding uneven rhythm from late changes

Using foot tapping to lock tempo
Using the Beginner Song Course app for rhythm practice
Developing chord-change timing while learning new songs
Managing early learning ‘fumble fest’ with patience
Final guidance: sound sweet on beat 1 to enhance musicality

sections.title: Strumming & Changing chords
sections.description: Justin states the core rule: for any song, aim to have the chord changes prepared so the strum lands on beat 1. If a change isn’t ready yet, adjust by starting the change early enough so the next strum lands on beat 1, prioritizing a clean, downbeat strum over perfect speed.
